## docs/ONBOARDING.md

Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/ONBOARDING.md

# Start using Lixity

Lixity helps you explore sentence rhythm, vocabulary and style patterns in a
Markdown manuscript on your computer. These signals point to passages worth
reviewing; they do not measure literary quality or prescribe edits.

Install Lixity using the [installation guide](INSTALLATION.md). Lixity is open
source under AGPL-3.0-or-later, so any writing purpose — private, research or
commercial — needs no extra permission; see [Licensing](LICENSING.md).

## The journey at a glance

| Stage | Where it happens | Continue with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| See a finished example | Browser, no installation | [Read-only demo](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/demo/report.html) · [Effi Briest](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/examples/effi-briest.html) · [Pride and Prejudice](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/examples/pride-and-prejudice.html) |
| Install and start | Terminal, then the local browser | [Installation guide](INSTALLATION.md) · [Use the interactive workspace](#use-the-interactive-workspace) |
| Choose a project | Welcome screen or workspace bar | [Choose your starting point](#choose-your-starting-point) · [Open or import?](#open-or-import) |
| First analysis | **Manuscript & Analysis** | [Read and explore](#read-and-explore) |
| Review notes | Flagged passages and paragraphs | [Work through review notes](#work-through-review-notes) |
| Research | **Research & Dossiers** | [Research workflow](#research-workflow) |
| Export and return | PDF export, then restart later | [Check your first session and return later](#check-your-first-session-and-return-later) |

## See a finished example first

Two public-domain novels are published as finished analyses: the
[Effi Briest example](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/examples/effi-briest.html)
(German) and the
[Pride and Prejudice example](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/examples/pride-and-prejudice.html)
(English) each pair an interactive excerpt with a complete PDF report. Both run
in the browser without installation; nothing is uploaded and nothing is saved
there. The [read-only synthetic demo](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/demo/report.html)
stays the smallest introduction. The local app's welcome screen links the
example that matches its analysis language.

## Choose your starting point

| What you want to do | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Explore a manuscript | Build a dashboard using the commands below. |
| Return to an existing project | Start the app and choose **Open Project**. |
| Start a project | Run `lixity service start --open` and choose **Analyze a manuscript** or **New Project**. |
| Keep research sources | Open an initialized research project, or initialize one as shown below. |
| Capture sources from Zotero | Follow the [Zotero setup](research/USAGE.md#zotero-desktop-bridge-since-v1190), then select attachments in the dashboard. |

## Start with a manuscript

Save your manuscript as a UTF-8 Markdown file. Use `## Chapter title` headings
and blank lines between paragraphs. From its folder, run:

```sh
lixity analyze manuscript.md --language en
lixity build manuscript.md --language en
```

Open `exports/manuscript_dashboard.html` in your browser. `analyze` gives a
terminal report; `build` saves the dashboard and other analysis reports in
`exports/`. The original manuscript stays in its project folder.

Choose the language of your manuscript: use `--language de` for German or
`--language en` for English. English is the default. Explicit
`--language auto` requests detection; weak or ambiguous evidence uses the
generic profile. German and English currently have the most extensive
linguistic resources and tests; other supported profiles have more limited
coverage. See [language support and limitations](LOCALIZATION.md).

Start with a longer passage and several chapters when possible. Some results
are unavailable for short texts or chapters without measurable variation. Read
the [interpretation guide](guides/interpretation.html) before treating a
highlight as a reason to revise.

## Use the interactive workspace

```sh
lixity service start --open
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. The workspace has three views:
**Research & Dossiers**, **Manuscript & Analysis**, and **Project & Settings**.
Since v2.3.0, the welcome guidance follows three steps: choose or open a
manuscript, confirm its language in the import preview, then read a passage behind
a signal. **Analyze a manuscript** opens the existing import dialog; analysis
starts after you confirm the preview. **Research and further analysis** expands
optional guidance. An empty manuscript view offers the same import action.
**New Project**, **Open Project** and optional welcome guidance remain available
in every view. Hide the guidance when you no longer need it; **Show guidance**
reopens it. The browser remembers this preference when local storage is available.

With the service stopped, `lixity service start --open ./my-novel` starts with
an explicit project instead. The managed service does not need an open terminal.
Its default startup is an empty workspace; it does not search your terminal's
folder. Use `lixity service status`, `lixity service restart` and
`lixity service stop` to manage the instance.

### Open or import?

**Open Project** reconnects an existing folder and its research archive. Enter
a folder or manuscript path, or use **Browse files and folders**. The chooser
shows files on the computer running Lixity. **Home** and **Parent folder** help
you navigate; choose a manuscript or **Select this folder**, then **Open**.
Browsing or cancelling does not switch projects.

**New Project → Import Manuscript** creates a separate project from a selected
or dropped `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` file. It does not reopen the original
folder or its research. Selecting a file opens its preview directly; the dialog
explains the next step in one line and asks only for what it needs: the project
title (prefilled from the first heading), the analysis language with its effect
named, and an optional **Author name** used for PDF credits, the title page and
the NDA. The project folder and the optional research archive stay under
**Optional details** with sensible defaults. Nothing is uploaded or written
outside the chosen folder. Confirm the new project in the import dialog.
**Start New Manuscript** follows the same pattern: title, language, optional
author, then the narrative template. The Research Novel template also
initializes a research archive.

An initialized research-only folder can be opened without a manuscript. Its
sources and notes remain available; manuscript analysis and comparison need a
loaded manuscript. All browser tabs connected to one server share its active
project, so check the displayed path when switching.

### Read and explore

**Since v0.3.0:** the native workspace offers a collapsed manuscript PDF menu
in the global project controls above all three views. Select
**A5 reading copy** (the default), **A4 manuscript sheets** or **A4 analysis report**,
then select **Download PDF** to save it. It generates a PDF from the currently selected
manuscript and returns it through your browser; it creates no server export files
and changes neither the manuscript nor the research archive. The form needs
JavaScript and a compatible live native server; standalone HTML reports do not
provide the download action.
The [`lixity pdf`](USAGE.md#lixity-pdf) terminal command remains available.

The **Start your review** panel appears before the measurements. **Open passage**
opens the first paragraph in source order that meets the selected tense-flag
threshold, or the opening paragraph when none does. It clears manuscript search
and paragraph filters so the text is visible, and moves keyboard focus to the
opened paragraph. This is a place to begin reading, not a quality ranking.

**Explore chapters** opens the style comparison when it is available; otherwise
it opens the chapter map with an explanation of the comparison's limits.
**Open sentence rhythm** is offered when measurements are available. Read the
passage before drawing conclusions from either view. Paragraph text appears
first; expand **Values** for source lines and measurements.

The manuscript view provides chapter and paragraph navigation, style signals
and analysis controls. Dotted-underlined terms have explanations: hover, use
keyboard focus, or tap. Press Escape or tap again to dismiss them. Statistical
settings also show their explanations beside the fields.

A saved HTML dashboard is a read-only analysis export. The local server adds
project and research actions using the same analysis engine. It is not a full
manuscript editor. The NDA generator downloads a friendly confidentiality agreement
using the recipient's name,
optional address, project, date and place; see the
[NDA reference](USAGE.md#nda-agreements).
Set **Author name** in the loaded project's Settings to prefill the project
representative in the agreement. Apply stores that name in the project. The
read-only manuscript identity check shows matching, missing or different metadata;
it does not edit prose or establish who wrote the text.
Book-specific publication and delivery integrations belong to project adapters;
the shared manuscript PDF layouts are described in the [PDF reference](USAGE.md#lixity-pdf).

## Work through review notes

The editorial loop starts where the measurements point and ends in the
manuscript:

1. Open the flagged passages list (or any paragraph) and read the excerpt it
   shows.
2. Open the paragraph. The text comes first; expand **Values** for source
   lines, tense labels and the compact measurement line.
3. Use the marker buttons (**Check**, **Fact-check**, **To-do**, **Attention**)
   to write a note directly on the passage. Nothing is saved until you choose
   **Save marker**; cancelling leaves the text unchanged.
4. Saved markers live as Markdown comments above their paragraph and stay
   visible in the marker list. Their visibility in a book export depends on the
   editor or converter you use.

Markers are your decisions: the analysis neither rewrites prose nor resolves a
flagged passage. See [work markers](USAGE.md#work-markers-editor-visible) and the
[editorial-loop walkthrough](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/#editorial-matrix).

## Research workflow

The research workspace is experimental. It keeps sources, quotations and authored
notes separate from manuscript analysis. Import a source only when you are
allowed to retain its original bytes. Retention does not grant redistribution
rights or verify a historical claim.

To initialize a new research archive and retain an authorized text source:

```sh
lixity research init --project ./my-novel --title "Novel research" --language en
lixity research ingest --project ./my-novel --file ./source.txt \
  --allow-retention --title "Library note"
lixity research search --project ./my-novel --query "reading room"
```

Research commands stay project-scoped. Since v2.4.0, the CLI also
accepts the validated initialized current directory for existing-archive commands;
it searches no parent folders or last-opened projects. Use `--project` when
working from elsewhere; it remains authoritative. See [CLI selection and the
link shortcut](research/USAGE.md#reading-and-cli-workflows-since-v240).
Search updates a stale search index
automatically unless `--strict` is requested. CLI search defaults to source
passages; `--scope all` also searches current dossiers, claims and decisions.
The dashboard searches all these record types by default. Only source passages
can be cited as evidence.

In the dashboard, select a source or dossier to read its details and citations.
Source and dossier filters narrow the loaded lists; **Search** looks through
retained text. A source-passage search result offers **Use for claim** and
**Use for dossier** actions.

**Since v2.4.0:** select text inside one source paragraph to prepare
a claim evidence-link draft. Read the selected quote and complete paragraph
context in the preview, choose the claim and evidence relation, then save
explicitly. The citation retains the whole source paragraph; selecting a
sentence does not create a sentence-level citation. Cross-paragraph or ambiguous
selections are unavailable; whole-passage actions remain in the Passages view.

Open **Dossier alongside** in **Manuscript & Analysis** and choose a dossier,
or use the matching action on a dossier card. Opening the optional view alone
does not choose a dossier. It is read-only, and closing it preserves manuscript
search and open paragraphs. Other analysis panels are temporarily hidden in this
focused reading view and return when you close it. Refresh explicitly for the latest saved dossier
revision; the selection lasts for the current page. The dossier appears above
the manuscript on narrow screens. Evidence status labels express your own
assessment; they do not certify historical facts.

For a visual reference, open a dossier and choose **Add image**. Select an
authorized local PNG/JPEG, add a short description, preview it and confirm
retention before saving. Original bytes and the dossier version are saved together.
Image sources have no searchable text or linguistic scores. Optional captions and
source notes help you remember what the picture can—and cannot—support.

Use **Add claim** or **Add decision** from that dossier to keep the topic selected
in the existing form. **Edit section** limits a revision to one unique heading;
you still review conflicts and explain the change before saving.

The records have different purposes:

- A **source** is retained evidence; its passages support exact quotations.
- A **dossier** collects notes, sections and cited passages on a topic.
- A **claim** records an assertion or hypothesis and an author-selected confidence
  label. Evidence links describe whether a passage supports, contradicts,
  qualifies or provides context for it.
- A **decision** records an author's choice and rationale. A linked dossier is
  marked for review when subsequent decisions are recorded.

These links support review, not automated proof. An unmarked deviation from fact
does not certify accuracy. If a source is purged, affected citations in retained
authored records show as unavailable rather than revealing deleted text.
**Since v3.0.0:** in **Claims**, switch from **List** to **Timeline**
to organize the period labels you entered. Clear years, dates and supported
ranges can be placed; unclear or invalid periods stay visible separately.
Placement is an organizational aid, not a historical verification.

Under **Cause and effect claims**, choose two reviewed claim versions and save
your proposed cause/effect link explicitly. Later claim edits leave that link
pinned to its earlier versions and mark it for review. Edit or retract it through
the shared revision editor; history keeps the earlier interpretation. Before the
first save, back up the archive and read the v6 compatibility notice: afterward
every reader must support archive schema v6: v0.3.0 and the
historical v3.0.x releases do. Product and archive versions are independent.

To add evidence without copying an identifier, choose your claim in the evidence
form and select **Find source passage**. Search, read a result, choose **Use for
claim**, then review its full retained paragraph and save the evidence relation.
A keyword match or causal interpretation does not verify a claim. A changed
reviewed context requires another review before saving.

Saved manuscript associations—a selected quote linked to a claim—are listed in
the research **Review** tab with their anchor state and review flags. A moved,
changed or ambiguous anchor stays unresolved and is never repinned silently;
listing them never writes.

See [Research usage](research/USAGE.md) for batch import, claim and decision
commands, backups and archive limits.

## Use Zotero for sources and media (since v1.19.0)

Zotero can remain your catalogue for books, PDFs and other media. Lixity captures
selected PDF/text attachments so that a later change in Zotero does not silently
change an earlier quotation. Images, audio and video stay in Zotero; Lixity does
not transcribe them. Scanned PDFs need local Tesseract or a configured OCR worker.

### First Zotero capture

Install Zotero on the computer running Lixity, enable its local API and download
the attachments you need. In **Research → Sources → Zotero**, choose the intended
library and collection, inspect an item, select an attachment and confirm
retention. Review its details and check a quotation against the original.

Before using an existing archive with a newer capture format, back it up and keep
all archive readers and writers on a compatible version. Follow the
[Zotero setup, migration and backup reference](research/USAGE.md#zotero-desktop-bridge-since-v1190)
for dry-run previews, explicit refresh and export. Capturing sources does not
enable automatic synchronization.

## Check your first session and return later

Before relying on a workspace, check its displayed project path, manuscript
language and a sample quotation against the source. For Zotero captures, also
check the original-item link and metadata. A successful search does not verify
a claim.

Stop the managed instance with `lixity service stop`. To return, run
`lixity service start --open` and open the existing project, or pass an explicit
project path when starting. Restart uses its recorded launch settings, so a
different project selected in the live browser does not change its startup
project. After updates or OCR setting changes, restart the intended instance;
a browser reload alone does not load updated code. A foreground `lixity serve`
still stops with Ctrl+C. See [server setup and restart](INSTALLATION.md#running-the-server).

Back up the manuscript separately from the research archive. Paired
research/Zotero backups exclude manuscripts and external linked attachments.
The [research command reference](research/USAGE.md) describes implemented
behavior; the [research RFC](research/README.md) also contains future proposals.

===============================================================================
## docs/INSTALLATION.md

Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md

# Install, verify and update Lixity

Lixity runs on your computer on Linux, macOS and Windows. It is
**open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later**. Install the published package
(`lixity` on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/lixity/)) or the pinned release
wheel with the commands below. Any writing purpose is covered;
a separate written commercial license exists only for closed-source
integrations. See [licensing](LICENSING.md) before installation.
Analysis runs offline; downloading Python, the package and dependencies requires
network access. No manuscript upload, account or API key is required.

## Where Lixity is published

| Channel | Use it for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [`lixity` on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/lixity/) | normal install and upgrades | `uv tool install lixity`; pipx and pip work as well |
| [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/releases) | pinned, checksum-verified setups | wheel, sdist and `SHA256SUMS`; build attestations via `gh attestation verify` |
| Zenodo | citing a released version | releases are archived automatically; concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.23390297` (see [`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/CITATION.cff)) |

Use the isolated **uv tool** installation for the application and CLI. Install
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) first if needed.
uv installs the published release wheel and supplies managed Python 3.12;
neither Git nor a separate Python installation is needed for this route.
The engine supports Python 3.10 or newer. Python API and editable developer
environments are [separate advanced routes](#python-api-project-environment).

## CLI: current release

These commands work in a terminal, including Windows PowerShell:

```sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 --managed-python lixity
uv tool update-shell
```

Open a new terminal, then verify and start the app:

```sh
lixity --version
lixity service start --open
```

The current release is **v0.4.6**. Read the [release notes](releases/v0.4.6.md)
for changes and compatibility information. For a reproducible, checksum-verified
setup, install the pinned release wheel instead (the release page also carries
`SHA256SUMS`):

```sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 --managed-python --reinstall-package lixity "https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/releases/download/v0.4.6/lixity-0.4.6-py3-none-any.whl"
```

`uv tool update-shell` configures shell integration once; it does not change an
already open terminal. **Open Project** reconnects an existing
manuscript folder; **Analyze a manuscript** opens the import preview. The default
service starts without a project and does not search the terminal's directory.
`uv tool list` shows the installed source. A tool installation does not make
`import lixity` available to a different Python environment.

This uses uv's [isolated tool environment](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/tools/)
and [managed Python support](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/python-versions/#requiring-or-disabling-managed-python-versions).
uv accepts [HTTPS wheel sources](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/dependencies/#url).

### Optional research prerequisites

<details>
<summary>PDF/OCR and Zotero setup for research</summary>

The experimental research workspace is included. Text and Markdown sources need
no OCR setup. Search needs SQLite with FTS5 support. Text PDFs need Poppler;
image-only scans need locally installed Tesseract or a configured OCR worker. See
[PDF and OCR setup](#server-environment-and-project-access).

For Zotero capture, install Zotero 10 or later on the same computer and enable
its local API in Settings → Advanced. Lixity reads `127.0.0.1:23119`; it does
not install or launch Zotero, modify its database or configure synchronization.
No cloud account is needed.
See the [Zotero setup and migration reference](research/USAGE.md#zotero-desktop-bridge-since-v1190).
Back up existing archives before creating v3 captures and use compatible versions
for all readers and writers. Installing Lixity does not download an OCR model.

</details>

### Development builds instead

<details>
<summary>Follow unreleased source changes</summary>

To follow unreleased changes, install [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads), then
use this **instead**:

```sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 --managed-python --reinstall-package lixity "git+https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity.git@main"
```

`main` changes over time. Review
[release notes](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/releases) before switching.
Stop the managed service before replacing its installation, verify the new
version, then start it again. This does not alter manuscript files.

</details>

### Updates and removal

Version 0.3.0 reset the product number to reflect development maturity before
1.0 while retaining existing features and historical releases. Notes written
before the renumbering may mention product versions such as 1.18.0 or
3.0.1; they describe the same product. Historical tags
such as 3.0.1 sort higher than the 0.4.x line in a numeric comparison; PyPI
carries only the 0.4.x line, and `uv tool upgrade lixity` moves forward inside
it. When choosing files on the release page, select the exact 0.4.x release.
Do not rely on a product-number comparison for archive compatibility. The
0.3.x/0.4.x line reads research schemas v1–v7; historical v3.0.1 cannot read
opt-in manuscript-link v7 archives. Installing new files does not restart a
running workspace; restart explicitly after the upgrade.

When upgrading from a historical build before v2.4.0, stop its instance through the
original foreground terminal (Ctrl+C), checkout launcher or configured OS
manager before replacing the installation. That version has no `service`
command, and the new controller deliberately does not adopt its process.

```sh
lixity service stop
uv tool upgrade lixity
lixity --version
lixity service start --open
```

`uv tool upgrade lixity` selects the newest published release when the tool came
from PyPI. A tool installed from a pinned wheel keeps that fixed URL — replace it
with `uv tool install --reinstall-package lixity` and the new wheel URL.
`--reinstall-package lixity` refreshes that package without forcing ownership
of another installer's entrypoint. See the official
[tool update reference](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-tool-install).
If you start with an explicit project, pass that path again after updating.

Before updates or removal, stop each managed instance using its port, for example
`lixity service stop --port 9000` for a custom-port instance. Before removal,
disable any login-startup entry you configured under systemd, launchd or Task
Scheduler. Then remove only Lixity:

```sh
lixity service stop
uv tool uninstall lixity
```

This removes the isolated tool installation, not your manuscript folders or
research archives. Keep shared uv and Python installations used by other tools.
Externally configured startup entries use their [own manager](#optional-startup-at-login).

If a terminal reports an older version than your checkout, compare `lixity
--version` with `.venv/bin/lixity --version` (`.venv\Scripts\lixity.exe --version`
on Windows). They may be separate installations. Use `command -v lixity` on
Linux/macOS or `Get-Command lixity` in PowerShell, then inspect `uv tool list`.
A non-editable tool installed from a local folder is a copy: changing the
folder does not update the installed tool. Reinstall the chosen release or
development source explicitly, verify its version, and restart its service.

<details>
<summary>Alternative for existing pipx users</summary>

If you already use pipx, install the published package with `pipx install lixity`
(or the pinned wheel URL for an exact release), then use `pipx ensurepath` if
necessary. Keep using that installer to replace or
remove its installation rather than overwriting its executable with uv.

</details>

## First useful result

The installed app opens an empty workspace. Choose **Analyze a manuscript**,
confirm its preview language and read the first linked passage. To return to a
saved folder, choose **Open Project**. See [Onboarding](ONBOARDING.md).

<details>
<summary>Generate an offline report from the CLI</summary>

Create a UTF-8 Markdown file named `manuscript.md` in your manuscript folder.
Use `## Chapter title` headings and blank lines between paragraphs. Then run:

```sh
lixity analyze manuscript.md --language en
lixity build manuscript.md --language en
```

Open `exports/manuscript_dashboard.html` in your browser. The build also saves
metrics and written reports. Very short texts cannot support a meaningful style
reference; unavailable results are expected.

Use `--language de` for German, or explicit `--language auto` for detection.
English is the default. A local `lixity.toml` can hold:

```toml
language = "de"
title = "My manuscript"
```

**Since v0.3.0:** selected-project title, `author_name` and an
optional `[publication]` table feed the shared CLI/native PDF composer. No new
renderer, runtime dependency or EPUB exporter is installed.
See [publication configuration and limits](USAGE.md#publication-settings).

For interactive project and research workflows, run `lixity service start --open`
and choose your project in the workspace. The standalone HTML
export remains read-only. The server's persistent workspace bar offers
**Open Project** for an existing folder and its research archive, and
**New Project → Import Manuscript** to create a separate project from uploaded text.
See [Onboarding](ONBOARDING.md) for this workflow. Since 2.0.0, the workspace includes a five-field NDA generator with preview and PDF/editable-text
downloads in the project language; see [NDA guidance](USAGE.md#nda-agreements).
It creates no server files or recipient registry. For characters outside the
native Windows-1252 PDF repertoire, download UTF-8 text for your local editor.

</details>

## Running the server

Use the packaged service controller from any terminal; no source checkout is
needed. It starts the same Python installation that provides your `lixity`
command and checks its managed instance before reporting readiness.

```sh
lixity service start --open
lixity service status
lixity service restart
lixity service stop
```

The default address is `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. Start uses an empty workspace
in an application-owned working directory, rather than discovering a manuscript
in your terminal's current folder. An explicit `LIXITY_DIR` also chooses a startup
project. With the service stopped, you can choose an
explicit project and another port:

```sh
lixity service start --open --port 9000 ./my-novel
lixity service status --port 9000
lixity service stop --port 9000
```

Linux uses a user systemd manager when available; other supported environments
use the detached-process backend. Login startup remains a separate explicit
choice. The controller manages instances it created, not arbitrary foreground
servers or external startup units. If another process owns the port, identify
that instance or choose another port; do not assume the controller owns it.

All tabs connected to one server share its active project. **Open Project**
changes that live workspace; CLI analysis, research and build commands do not.
`start` uses fresh launch settings. `restart` uses recorded launch settings plus
explicit overrides, even after a stop; a project selected later in the browser
does not replace the startup project. After updates or OCR environment
changes, restart the appropriate managed instance; a browser reload alone does
not load new code. Supply OCR variables in the new start/restart environment;
their values are not saved as launch settings.

Since v3.0.1, foreground `serve` and managed start/restart accept
`--min-chapters N` (an integer of at least 2, default 2). Restart retains the
saved threshold unless overridden; see the [service command reference](USAGE.md#lixity-service).

<details>
<summary>Backend selection, stored launch settings and logs</summary>

`--backend auto` prefers an available Linux user systemd manager and otherwise
uses a detached process. `--backend process` explicitly chooses the latter;
`--backend systemd` fails when no usable user manager exists. These managed units
are transient and do not enable startup at login. Backend selection applies to
each invocation and is not saved: repeat `--backend process` on restart to keep
that choice; otherwise restart uses `auto`. `lixity service status --json`
reports readiness, installed/running versions, backend and log path; see the
[command contract](USAGE.md#lixity-service) for states and exit codes.

Saved launch settings and `service-PORT.log` live separately from the package:

| Platform | Default state folder |
| --- | --- |
| Linux | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/lixity/service`, or `~/.local/state/lixity/service` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/lixity/service` |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lixity\service` |

Runtime records use `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/lixity-service` when set, otherwise
`runtime/lixity-service` inside that state folder. `LIXITY_SERVICE_STATE_DIR`
and `LIXITY_SERVICE_RUNTIME_DIR` explicitly override these locations. Stop
retains launch settings and logs; uv uninstall removes the tool environment,
leaving application state and user imports intact. There is no cleanup command
that deletes project storage.

</details>

For a foreground server, including development and embedding use, keep the
existing command and stop it with Ctrl+C:

```sh
lixity serve --no-project --open
```

`lixity service stop` does not stop an unrelated foreground `serve` process.
The same CLI is available as `python -m lixity` in an environment containing
Lixity. From a source checkout, `scripts/lixity-start.sh`,
`scripts/lixity-start.ps1` and `make serve` / `make stop` delegate to this shared
controller; they are compatibility entrypoints, not separate lifecycle engines.

### Optional startup at login

<details>
<summary>Explicit Linux, macOS and Windows startup managers</summary>

Use these advanced options only when you want startup at login. They do not
replace the primary service workflow. A unit or task you configure independently
is managed and disabled with its own OS manager before removal or replacement.
The template commands assume a source checkout, or that you saved the linked
templates in a `scripts/` folder. Stop the managed instance on the chosen port
before enabling a separate login-startup entry.

### Auto-start on login — Linux (systemd user service)

Optional: use the [systemd template](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/scripts/lixity.service)
to start at login. Edit its executable path and project directory before enabling it:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp scripts/lixity.service ~/.config/systemd/user/lixity.service

# Edit ExecStart to point to your lixity binary (check: which lixity)
nano ~/.config/systemd/user/lixity.service

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now lixity    # enable + start immediately

# Management
systemctl --user status  lixity
systemctl --user restart lixity
journalctl --user -u lixity -f          # live log

# Disable login startup before removing the installation
systemctl --user disable --now lixity
```

The template explains port changes and service options. If you deliberately
need it running without a login session, use `loginctl enable-linger $USER`.
The service must be able to write to its project folder.

### Auto-start on login — macOS (launchd agent)

Optional: edit the [launchd template](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/scripts/lixity.plist)
to point to your executable. To preload a project, replace `--no-project` in its
ProgramArguments with the explicit project path, then register it:

```sh
# Edit the plist: set the correct path to your lixity binary (check: which lixity)
# and choose an explicit startup project only if wanted.
nano scripts/lixity.plist

cp scripts/lixity.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.lixity.serve.plist
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.lixity.serve.plist

# Management
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.lixity.serve   # restart
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.lixity.serve        # stop and unload
tail -f /tmp/lixity-stdout.log                        # live log

# Disable auto-start
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.lixity.serve
launchctl disable gui/$(id -u)/com.lixity.serve
```

### Auto-start on login — Windows (Task Scheduler)

Optional: register the installed foreground server in Task Scheduler to start
at login. Use its executable directly; no PowerShell launcher or execution-policy
change is needed:

```powershell
$binary    = (Get-Command lixity -CommandType Application).Source
$action    = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $binary `
              -Argument "serve --no-project --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765"
$trigger   = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn -User $env:USERNAME
$settings  = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -ExecutionTimeLimit 0 -RestartCount 3 -RestartInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 1)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Lixity Dashboard" `
    -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings -RunLevel Limited
```

Manage it from Task Scheduler GUI (`taskschd.msc`) or PowerShell:

```powershell
Start-ScheduledTask  -TaskName "Lixity Dashboard"
Stop-ScheduledTask   -TaskName "Lixity Dashboard"
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Lixity Dashboard" -Confirm:$false  # remove
```

</details>

### After a computer restart (quick reference)

Run `lixity service start --open` again, or use your explicitly configured
login-startup manager. Your project remains in its folder;
reinstallation or reimport is unnecessary. Reapply any OCR environment settings,
which are not saved in project settings. Start Zotero for new captures;
retained evidence stays readable while it is closed.

## Python API: project environment

These advanced source installs require Git and an existing Python 3.10+.

Linux/macOS:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity.git@v0.4.6"
.venv/bin/python -m pip check
.venv/bin/python -c "import lixity; print(lixity.__version__)"
```

Windows PowerShell (no activation or execution-policy change needed):

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install "git+https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity.git@v0.4.6"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip check
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import lixity; print(lixity.__version__)"
```

Use the same environment's `python -m pip install --upgrade` command and
explicit source URL to update. Do not update an unrelated global Python.

## Editable checkout

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity.git
cd lixity
make install-dev
make check
```

On Linux/macOS, `make install` creates `.venv` without development tools;
both installation targets check dependency compatibility and print the version.
Neither changes the global Python installation. You can select another
environment using `VENV=/path/to/environment` and interpreter using `PYTHON=python3.12`.

Without make, create the environment as above and use its Python to run
`-m pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then `-m pip check` and `-m pytest -W error -q -p no:asyncio`.
Keep an editable engine checkout separate from manuscript folders; reuse the
package rather than copying engine code into every book project.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `uv` not found | Install uv and reopen the terminal. Git is needed only for source installs. |
| `lixity` not found | Use `uv tool update-shell`, or the chosen venv's executable directly. |
| `externally-managed-environment` | Use `uv tool` or a venv; do not use `--break-system-packages`. |
| Project settings ignored | Check `lixity.toml` syntax and the selected project path; explicit CLI flags take precedence. |
| Wrong version or old controls after update | Check `uv tool list` and `command -v lixity` (PowerShell: `Get-Command lixity`), then stop the old server and restart on the same port. Check that the browser uses that address. |
| Dependency build error | Try a supported CPython version with binary wheels, e.g. 3.12; retain the full installer error. |
| HTML lacks project or research actions | A standalone export is read-only. Use `lixity service start --open` for the local workspace and PDF/NDA download actions. |

## Optional shell completion

Bash:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions
lixity completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/lixity
```

For Zsh, generate `_lixity` in a **user-writable directory on `$fpath`** and
initialize completion with `autoload -Uz compinit; compinit`. Do not assume
the first existing `$fpath` directory is writable.

See the [usage reference](USAGE.md), [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[contributor guide](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the next steps.

## Server environment and project access

The folder browser sees files available to the server process. A service account,
container or sandbox may have different access from your terminal. If a project
cannot be opened, check the process user, folder permissions and mounted paths.
Use **Open Project** to reconnect the original archive rather than importing
another copy. Keep private project data outside the engine checkout.

For PDF import, make `pdftotext` and `pdftoppm` available in that same environment.
Debian/Ubuntu package: `poppler-utils`; Homebrew package: `poppler`.
Run `lixity research ocr-status` to check configuration. Image-only scans need
local Tesseract and selected language data, or a configured `LIXITY_OCR_WORKER`.
Set `LIXITY_OCR_BACKEND=tesseract` for local recognition. `deu+eng` is an example
German/English language selection; choose the actual scan languages in
`LIXITY_OCR_LANGUAGES`. Restart the server manually with those environment values.

Since 2.0.0, **Research → Set up OCR and Zotero** offers an explicit
metadata-only check even before opening a project. It installs nothing and writes
no configuration. A reachable Zotero API does not establish library, collection
or attachment access; those remain separate explicit browse actions.
See [the extraction contract](research/USAGE.md#self-hosted-pdf-and-ocr-extraction).
The [Unlimited-OCR integration guide](research/OCR_INTEGRATION.md) describes the
external-worker boundary and the limited historical CPU experiment. Upstream
`infer.py` cannot be used directly as a `LIXITY_OCR_WORKER` executable.

The [browser installation guide](https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/guides/installation.html)
provides a synthetic first-dashboard example and links to interpretation and
source/PDF workflows.

## docs/USAGE.md
